blocks.explanation:
Yeh series G.P. nahi hai: \(\frac{0.22}{0.2} = 1.1\) lekin \(\frac{0.222}{0.22} \approx 1.009\); ratio barabar nahi.
Trick: 2 bahar nikalein, phir 9 se multiply aur divide karein; is se har term "1 minus \(\frac{1}{10}\) ki koi power" ban jata hai.
Plan: series ko "\(n\) ones" minus ek G.P. mein tod kar G.P. ka sum lagayenge.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(0.2 + 0.22 + 0.222 + \cdots\), \(n\) terms tak.
Humein find karna hai: \(S_n\).
Tareeqa: Har term ko aise likhenge ke andar se G.P. nikal aaye, phir \(S_n = \frac{a_1(1 - r^{n})}{1 - r}\) lagayenge. Yeh repeated digits (dohraye hue hindson) wali series ka standard tareeqa hai.

Common factor 2 bahar nikalein
\[S_n = 2(0.1 + 0.11 + 0.111 + \cdots)\]
Kyun: Har term mein sirf 2 ka digit dohraya gaya hai: \(0.2 = 2 \times 0.1\), \(0.22 = 2 \times 0.11\). Bahar nikalne se andar sirf 1 wale numbers reh jate hain, jin par kaam karna aasan hai.

9 se multiply aur divide karein
\[S_n = \dfrac{2}{9}(0.9 + 0.99 + 0.999 + \cdots)\]
Kyun: \(\frac{9}{9} = 1\) se multiply karne se qeemat nahi badalti. Faida yeh hai ke \(9 \times 0.1 = 0.9\), \(9 \times 0.11 = 0.99\), \(9 \times 0.111 = 0.999\): ab har term 1 ke bilkul qareeb hai.

Har term ko "1 minus chhota number" likhein
\[S_n = \dfrac{2}{9}\left[(1 - 0.1) + (1 - 0.01) + \cdots\right]\]
\[= \dfrac{2}{9}\left[n - (0.1 + 0.01 + \cdots)\right]\]
Kyun: \(0.9 = 1 - 0.1\), \(0.99 = 1 - 0.01\), \(0.999 = 1 - 0.001\). \(n\) terms hain, to \(n\) dafa 1 jama ho kar \(n\) bana, aur chhote numbers alag group ho gaye.
Dhyan dein: Chhote numbers ka group bhi \(n\) terms ka hai, \(n - 1\) ka nahi.

Andar wali G.P. ka sum
\[0.1 + 0.01 + \cdots = \dfrac{\frac{1}{10}\left(1 - \frac{1}{10^{n}}\right)}{1 - \frac{1}{10}}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{9}\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{10^{n}}\right)\]
Kyun: Yeh G.P. hai jis ka pehla term \(\frac{1}{10}\) aur ratio \(\frac{1}{10}\) hai (har term pichle ka dasvan hissa). Neeche \(1 - \frac{1}{10} = \frac{9}{10}\), aur \(\frac{1}{10} \div \frac{9}{10} = \frac{1}{9}\).

Wapas rakhein
\[S_n = \dfrac{2}{9}\left[n - \dfrac{1}{9}\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{10^{n}}\right)\right]\]
Kyun: Bracket wali G.P. ki jagah us ka sum rakh diya; yahi answer key wali shakal hai.

Tasdeeq: \(n = 2\)
\[\dfrac{2}{9}\left[2 - \dfrac{1}{9} \cdot \dfrac{99}{100}\right] = \dfrac{2}{9} \cdot \dfrac{189}{100}\]
\[= 0.42\]
Kyun: Pehle do terms ka sum \(0.2 + 0.22 = 0.42\) hai. Formula ne bhi 0.42 diya: \(\frac{1}{9} \cdot \frac{99}{100} = \frac{11}{100}\), \(2 - 0.11 = 1.89\), aur \(\frac{2}{9} \times 1.89 = 0.42\).

blocks.explanation:
Wohi trick jo (i) mein lagayi, bas ab whole numbers hain jin mein ek hi digit dohraya gaya hai.
Plan: 3 bahar nikalenge, 9 se multiply aur divide karenge taake terms \(10^{k} - 1\) ban jayein, phir 10 ki powers wali G.P. ka sum lenge.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(3 + 33 + 333 + \cdots\), \(n\) terms tak.
Humein find karna hai: \(S_n\).
Tareeqa: Yeh series bhi G.P. nahi (\(\frac{33}{3} = 11\), \(\frac{333}{33} \approx 10.09\)), is liye har term ko aise likhenge ke andar G.P. nazar aaye.

3 bahar nikalein, phir 9 se multiply aur divide karein
\[S_n = 3(1 + 11 + 111 + \cdots)\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{3}(9 + 99 + 999 + \cdots)\]
Kyun: \(33 = 3 \times 11\), \(333 = 3 \times 111\). Phir 9 se multiply: \(9 \times 11 = 99\), \(9 \times 111 = 999\). Bahar \(\frac{3}{9} = \frac{1}{3}\) bacha.

Har term ko "10 ki power minus 1" likhein
\[S_n = \dfrac{1}{3}\left[(10 - 1) + (10^{2} - 1) + \cdots + (10^{n} - 1)\right]\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{3}\left[(10 + 10^{2} + \cdots + 10^{n}) - n\right]\]
Kyun: \(9 = 10 - 1\), \(99 = 100 - 1 = 10^{2} - 1\), \(999 = 10^{3} - 1\). \(n\)th term \(10^{n} - 1\) hai. Saari powers ek group mein aur \(n\) dafa 1 doosre group mein, jo \(n\) banta hai.

10 ki powers wali G.P. ka sum
\[10 + 10^{2} + \cdots + 10^{n} = \dfrac{10(10^{n} - 1)}{10 - 1}\]
\[= \dfrac{10}{9}(10^{n} - 1)\]
Kyun: Pehla term 10, ratio 10, \(n\) terms. Jab \(r > 1\) ho to \(\frac{a_1(r^{n} - 1)}{r - 1}\) wali shakal behtar hai kyunke upar neeche dono positive rehte hain; yeh asal mein wohi formula hai, sirf upar neeche \(-1\) se multiply kiya hua.
Dhyan dein: Pehla term 10 hai, 1 nahi; isi liye upar \(10(10^{n} - 1)\) aaya.

Wapas rakhein
\[S_n = \dfrac{1}{3}\left[\dfrac{10}{9}(10^{n} - 1) - n\right]\]
Kyun: Powers ke group ki jagah us ka sum rakh diya.

Tasdeeq: \(n = 2\)
\[\dfrac{1}{3}\left[\dfrac{10}{9}(99) - 2\right] = \dfrac{1}{3}(110 - 2)\]
\[= 36\]
Kyun: \(3 + 33 = 36\), aur formula bhi 36 deta hai (\(\frac{10}{9} \times 99 = 110\)). Is liye jawab sahi hai.
